items.followUp: State the organism that causes malaria and the insect that transmits it.

rubric.why: Identifies the parasite responsible for malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Plasmodium or clearly identifying it as the malaria parasite.

rubric.why: Gives a further correct observation about how malaria spreads or its symptoms.
rubric.description: It is spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes; common symptoms include recurring fever and chills.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the transmitting mosquito or giving a characteristic symptom.

modelAnswer: Malaria is caused by a parasite of the genus Plasmodium.
It is transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito and commonly causes recurring fever with chills.

items.followUp: What is quinine, and what is its source?

rubric.description: Cinchona is a tree whose bark contains quinine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Cinchona as a tree or its bark as the source.

rubric.why: States the important medicinal product and its use.
rubric.description: Quinine obtained from the bark is used to treat malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming quinine and linking it to malaria treatment.

modelAnswer: Cinchona is a tree whose bark contains quinine.
Quinine is a medicine used to treat malaria.

items.followUp: How do ribosomes distinguish rough endoplasmic reticulum from smooth endoplasmic reticulum?

rubric.why: Identifies the feature that gives rough ER its appearance.
rubric.description: Rough endoplasmic reticulum has ribosomes attached to its surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ribosomes are attached to rough ER.

rubric.why: Identifies the distinguishing feature of smooth ER.
rubric.description: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum has no ribosomes attached to its surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that smooth ER lacks attached ribosomes.

modelAnswer: Rough endoplasmic reticulum has ribosomes attached to its surface, giving it a rough appearance.
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum has no attached ribosomes and therefore appears smooth.

items.followUp: State one function of chromoplasts and one function of leucoplasts.

rubric.why: States the pigment-related distinguishing feature of chromoplasts.
rubric.description: Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments and give colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromoplasts contain coloured pigments or provide colour.

rubric.why: States the lack of colour and storage role of leucoplasts.
rubric.description: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying leucoplasts as colourless or as food-storing plastids.

modelAnswer: Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments, which give colour to plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.

items.followUp: Name two organizations working to conserve wildlife in Pakistan.

accept: international union for conservation of nature
rubric.why: Names a recognized organization involved in biodiversity protection in Pakistan.
rubric.description: One mark is awarded for one correct organization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming WWF-Pakistan, IUCN-Pakistan, or another valid conservation organization.

accept: international union for conservation of nature
rubric.description: A second mark is awarded for a different correct organization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid organization; do not award twice for the same organization.

modelAnswer: IUCN-Pakistan also works for the protection of biodiversity.

items.followUp: Explain how predation by sea stars affects mussel populations and biodiversity.

rubric.why: Recognizes the feeding relationship between sea stars and mussels.
rubric.description: Sea stars are predators that feed on mussels, their prey.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sea stars as predators of mussels.

rubric.why: Explains the ecological effect of sea stars eating mussels.
rubric.description: By controlling mussel numbers, sea stars help maintain biodiversity and prevent mussels from dominating.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that predation controls mussel populations or helps maintain biodiversity.

modelAnswer: Sea stars are predators that eat mussels.
By controlling the mussel population, sea stars help prevent mussels from dominating and help maintain biodiversity.

items.followUp: Name four animals that live in the mountainous areas of Pakistan.

rubric.why: Credits the first two suitable animal names.
rubric.description: One mark for two correctly named animals of northern Pakistan.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two different suitable animals living in northern Pakistan.

rubric.why: Credits the next two suitable animal names.
rubric.description: One mark for two further correctly named animals of northern Pakistan.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two additional different suitable animals; the answer should contain four animals in total.

modelAnswer: Examples include the snow leopard, markhor, brown bear and Himalayan ibex.

items.followUp: Give two examples of how apoptosis benefits a multicellular organism.

rubric.why: States that apoptosis removes cells that are damaged or no longer needed.
rubric.description: Apoptosis removes damaged, abnormal or unnecessary cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct cell-removal role.

rubric.why: Gives a further benefit of programmed cell death.
rubric.description: Apoptosis supports normal development and tissue maintenance, and helps prevent abnormal cell growth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example or benefit, such as shaping tissues during development or helping prevent cancer.

modelAnswer: Apoptosis removes damaged, abnormal or unnecessary cells from the body.
It is important in normal development and tissue maintenance, and helps prevent abnormal cells from growing uncontrollably.
